articles.headline: Man City cheated because Premier League was built to be unfair
articles.description: The Premier League is unfair: Some teams are allowed to spend more than everyone else. So, of course Man City cheated to win.
articles.body:
Back in 1887, everyone was already playing soccer in England. The Premier League didn't exist -- nor did any other league. Instead, there was the Birmingham Cup, the Staffordshire Cup, the Lancashire Cup, the English Cup, the Welsh Cup, the FA Cup and plenty of other tournaments that were seemingly being created at random every other day.

The problem with the ad-hoc, knockout-only schedule is that, as the founder of the Football League William McGregor put it, there was no "fixity of fixtures." Teams would get knocked out of multiple tournaments early and have nowhere to play. Or they'd make a deep run in the FA Cup and have to cancel their games in Lancashire Cup because, how were they supposed to know they'd make it to the semifinals of the FA Cup?

Fans didn't love it either. McGregor said they "became disgusted by the intermittent fare provided for them."

Born in Scotland, McGregor emigrated to Birmingham around 1870. He owned a small drapery shop and eventually became an administrator for one of the leading, nascent football clubs in the area: Aston Villa.

"A great many people saw the difficulty which football and footballers were in; I happened, luckily, to be the one man at that particular time who saw the way out," he said, according to The Story of Association Football, written by J.A.H. Catton in 1926. "It appeared to me that a fixed program of home-and-home matches between the leading clubs in the country ... would produce football of a more interesting nature than the average game we saw."

In March 1888, McGregor suggested to five of the other leading clubs in England that they form a 12-team competition with this "fixity of fixtures." By September, the Football League played its first matches.

Historians initially suggested that McGregor came up with the idea of a "league" from cricket, the country's other most popular sport. However, as shown by Andrew Zimbalist and Stefan Szymanski, authors of "National Pastime: How Americans Play Baseball and the Rest of the World Plays Soccer," it seems more likely that McGregor was inspired by the success of baseball's National League over in the United States.

But the inspiration ended with the schedule. The National League was a closed system where the owners would only welcome new clubs if they all thought it would increase everyone's profits. Sport and business were tied together from the start.

Instead, the Football League accepted its place within the Football Association, England's larger governing body for the sport. From day one, league rules included language about the worst-performing teams being replaced by the best-performing teams from a lower league. The FA imposed a rule that no team directors could be paid for their services.

articles.headline: How the Knicks celebrated their long-awaited championship in the offseason
articles.description: From Jalen Brunson's SNL appearance to KAT's wedding, it all began with one event that turned into a domino effect: a Knicks title.
articles.body:
2026 was a season to remember for the New York Knicks, with the iconic franchise winning its first NBA championship in half a century.

As a welcome consequence of the title run, it was also a particularly long season for New York, stretching from October to mid-June. So when the offseason finally arrived, with a championship to celebrate, it was a safe bet the Knicks would make the most of it.

Make the most of it they did. From a euphoric Manhattan parade to "Saturday Night Live," the Knicks had one of the most memorable NBA offseasons in recent memory.

With New York's next regular season starting Tuesday, here's a look back at what the defending champions got up to over the summer.

A long-awaited parade

A unique quirk in New York City history meant that while the Knicks have won three NBA titles, the team had never had a ticker-tape parade. That changed in June, when the 2026 Knicks got their trip down the city's streets.

Unsurprisingly, it was a raucous event. Fans from across the New York metropolitan area flocked to the city well before sunrise to line up for a spot along the route, and attendance reached capacity three hours before the parade's scheduled start. Once the parade did get underway, it was one to remember, featuring a case of mistaken identity for Tyler Kolek, celebrity cameos and chants of "MVP" for the New York City Department of Sanitation.

Karl-Anthony Towns ties the knot

One Knicks star had some particularly important personal business to attend to over the offseason break.

Karl-Anthony Towns, who had proposed on Christmas Day the year prior, said "I do" with his now-wife, Jordyn Woods. The guest list for the star-studded couple's wedding was unsurprisingly packed -- in addition to Towns' New York teammates, Michael B. Jordan and Justin and Hailey Bieber were both reportedly in Malibu for the occasion.

Jalen Brunson hosts SNL

Season 52 of "Saturday Night Live" opened in September with a host familiar to city sports fans (and probably non-sports fans, too, at this point): star point guard Jalen Brunson.

But while Brunson was the host and guest actor in that night's skits, he wasn't alone in representing the team -- Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart were all in the audience for his monologue, with Brunson bantering with his teammates before they eventually joined him on stage at the segment's conclusion.

World Cup appearances

Beyond the NBA Finals, the FIFA World Cup was another event taking the world by storm, and it was part of the Knicks' championship tour.

Accessorized in sunglasses, Hart, Bridges and Anunoby sat in the New York Jets' suite at New York/New Jersey Stadium for France's match against Senegal just days after their win. When the trio appeared on the jumbotron, the stadium roared as Bridges pointed to his "New York" Knicks wordmarked hat. Hart was also on hand for England's win over Norway.

The Knicks ... they went international with it.

articles.headline: LeBron James' most notable Madison Square Garden appearances
articles.description: Here are some of LeBron James' memorable performances at the world's most famous arena throughout the years as he faces the Knicks on Tuesday.
articles.body:
LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers will travel to Madison Square Garden to face the New York Knicks on Tuesday in the season opener for both teams, which will also be James' debut with the Sixers.

James has played 34 games in the "World's Most Famous Arena," amassing a 24-10 record while averaging 28.1 points, 7.4 assists and 6.9 rebounds per game. 

He has met the Knicks only once in the postseason: the first round of the 2012 playoffs, which the Miami Heat won 4-1. He averaged 27.8 points, 6.2 rebounds and 5.6 assists, and scored less than 20 points only once in that series.

James has had his share of memorable games at Madison Square Garden throughout the years. Here's a look at some of the most notable.

Feb. 1, 2026: 22 points, 6 assists, 5 rebounds, 60% shooting

Game result:  112-100, Lakers loss

James had respectable numbers in his most recent trip to Madison Square Garden, shooting 60% from the field, and the Lakers were up on the Knicks heading into halftime. New York came roaring back, however, scoring 38 points to the Lakers' 26 in the third quarter and hanging on for a 12-point victory.

Earlier that day, James had been chosen as an All-Star reserve, making for an NBA-record 22nd consecutive appearance on the squad. The possibility of this being James' final game at the Garden sent prices soaring, with even the cheap seats going for $500.

Feb. 1, 2025: 33 points, 12 assists, 11 rebounds, 54% shooting

Game result:  128-112, Lakers win

James truly put on a show against the Knicks in 2025 with a memorable 30-point triple-double. He became the first visiting player with multiple 30-point triple-doubles at Madison Square Garden, including the playoffs. It was also James' 12th career 30-point game as a visiting player at MSG, breaking a tie with Kareem Abdul-Jabbar for second all time. 

There was no shortage of big plays from the then-40-year-old star that night, including a thunderous two-handed slam in the fourth quarter that left comedian Chris Rock stunned courtside. 

Although James' performance made headlines, it was overshadowed after the game when news broke of the shocking trade that sent Luka Doncic to the Lakers. 

Jan. 31, 2023: 28 points, 11 assists, 10 rebounds, 1 steal, 44% shooting

Game result:  129-123, Lakers win

Year 20 or not, James would never miss an opportunity to wow the New York crowd.

It was his first game there since January 2020, and James made it worth the wait. He had his first triple-double of the season as the Lakers squeaked out an overtime victory.

There was buzz heading into the game, with James weeks away from breaking the career scoring record. However, after the game, James focused on his all-around skills instead.

"I just play the game the right way. I approach the game every night only trying to be a triple threat by scoring, rebounding, assisting, defending, and may the chips fall where they may," he said.

Nov. 13, 2017: 23 points, 12 assists, 9 rebounds, 3 blocks, 50% shooting

articles.headline: James Maddison apologises to Coventry fans for Tottenham goal celebration
articles.description: James Maddison has apologised to the Coventry City fans for his goal celebration on Monday night.
articles.body:
James Maddison has apologised to the Coventry City fans for his goal celebration on Monday night.

Maddison opened the scoring for Tottenham Hotspur in their 3-1 win with a beautiful curling effort. It was his first start in 526 days after a serious knee injury and came against his first club from his hometown.

Maddison posted a picture alongside Coventry fans, holding up their shirt, on Tuesday to explain his actions while he celebrated.

"I had already planned my first goal back," he said via social media. "I was kissing the badge of this club who has supported me and my family through the darkest days of my career over the past 18 months.

"I absolutely adore and love Coventry City. All my close friends and family know that.

"I'm a fan and always will be and I will 100% apologise to anyone who thought the timing was bad as my first goal back just happened to be against my hometown club.

"Good luck to Frank [Lampard] and the boys for the rest of the season."

Maddison helped Tottenham claim their first Premier League win of the season, rising them from the foot of the table.

Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies were also on the scoresheet on a night which saw Dejan Kulusevski make his own long-anticipated comeback from a knee injury.

- Dejan Kulusevski explains why he is 'different' after Tottenham injury hell

- Tottenham left to mull cost of win over Coventry despite James Maddison, Dejan Kulusevski returns

- Maddison scores in 'dream' return as Spurs get 1st PL win of season

Maddison had returned from a damaged anterior cruciate ligament in April and had made a series of substitute appearances but started for the first time since against Coventry.

"Even though they've brought in a lot of attacking talent, he will still think no one's better than him because he's that type of character," pundit Jamie Carragher told Sky Sports about Maddison.

"He has that football arrogance that I like in players.

"It will be interesting to see where he fits in eventually because there are a lot of players at Tottenham in the attacking positions, especially with Kulusevski back."

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Bold predictions for the 2026-27 season
articles.description: Our fantasy hoops experts for their boldest predictions for the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
Separating yourself in fantasy basketball requires a strong draft and savvy moves on the waiver wire throughout the season. But it also takes some foresight -- seeing things before everyone else seems to.

With that in mind, we asked our fantasy hoops experts for their boldest predictions for the 2026-27 NBA season. If any of these come true, they could swing fantasy leagues in a big way.

Here are André Snellings, Eric Moody, Erik Karabell, Steve Alexander, Jim McCormick and Michael F. Florio with their hot takes.

Kel'el Ware finishes top 30 on the Player Rater

McCormick: Myles Turner represents real traffic for Ware, although the Milwaukee Bucks might be compelled to prioritize Ware's exposure given a massive advantage in rebounding on both sides of the court. For an otherwise undersized, wing-centric roster, Ware represents a key frontcourt building block from the Giannis package. There is overlap with Turner in trailing plays and protecting the rim, but I'm betting on talent and playing time to meet in Milwaukee this season.

Someone other than Nikola Jokic leads the league in fantasy points this season

Snellings: Jokic has led the league in total fantasy points for six straight seasons. Last season, Jokic led the league in fantasy scoring average as well -- enough so that he produced over 500 more fantasy points than second place, despite playing in just 65 games. This year, however, there are three players with a reasonable chance to overtake him.

Luka Doncic was second in fantasy points last season and, while he was a Maverick, had a season with a higher fantasy scoring average than Jokic (only in fewer games). With LeBron James no longer with the Lakers, Doncic could be in for his biggest fantasy season. Another contender, Victor Wembanyama, is coming off his best season and should still be improving at still only 22 years old. Finally, Giannis Antetokounmpo has historically produced seasons of similar scoring averages to Jokic and, with his new role on the Miami Heat, could produce one of his better fantasy seasons.

Julius Randle returns to being a top-25 player in points leagues

Florio: Randle is back as the top option on an offense, just as he was during his early days with the New York Knicks. Twice in a three year span, Randle averaged over 24 points per game. Over that time, he averaged at least 9.9 rebounds each year, while twice averaging over five assists per game. I also expect him to attempt more threes with the Brooklyn Nets, just like he did during his Knicks days. Once again the focal point of an offense, volume wins out and props him to another breakout fantasy basketball season.

articles.headline: José Mourinho on Vinícius Jr.: 'No player untouchable at Real Madrid'
articles.description: José Mourinho insisted that no player is "untouchable" at Real Madrid, as Vinícius Júnior prepares to return to the starting Xl for Wednesday's UCL match.
articles.body:
José Mourinho insisted that no player is "untouchable" at Real Madrid, as Vinícius Júnior prepares to return to the starting Xl for Wednesday's Champions League game with RB Leipzig.

Vinícius is currently serving a four-game ban in LaLiga and so is only available to play in Europe, where he made an underwhelming appearance away at Roma last week, being substituted on 58 minutes as his replacement, Endrick, inspired a 4-3 win.

Mourinho has consistently backed the Brazil international this season, despite a run of poor form which has seen him contribute just one goal for his club in all competitions, and competition for his place from Madrid's record summer signing, Yan Diomande.

"Only the badge is untouchable," Mourinho said in a news conference on Tuesday. "I don't like the concept of 'untouchable' players. What makes players untouchable isn't a captain's armband, or how long they've been at the club, or their status. What makes a player untouchable is performance."

Madrid are trailing leaders Barcelona by six points in LaLiga ahead of Sunday's Clásico at Camp Nou, but they have maximum points in the Champions League so far after two wins out of two against Inter Milan and Roma.

However Mourinho said his team couldn't be considered among the favourites to win this season's competition.

"It's very early," Mourinho said. "Right now Real Madrid don't have the objective of winning the Champions League. We have the objective of qualifying [for the knockout phase]. Then, if we get the points that allow us to qualify, then we get to our second objective, to try to avoid the playoffs, which are two games with tension, and they're games you can avoid."

Mourinho made changes to his team for Sunday's LaLiga game with Sevilla at the Bernabéu, playing Arda Güler in central midfield and giving starts to Diomande and Endrick, and was rewarded with a 4-1 win.

"As I said recently, I'm not a stubborn coach," Mourinho said. "There are coaches who have an idea, and live or die by that idea. I'm not that kind of coach, I'm always open to analyse, to understand things and look for the best for the team."

Defender Ibrahima Konaté said Mourinho has "an aura that not many managers have."

"He doesn't need to speak, and everyone will listen and respect him," Konaté said. "He's a great manager, and everyone here at this club wants success with him."

Konaté was also asked about an incident in September in which he, Kylian Mbappé and Vinicius refused to wear a pre-match T-shirt supporting the Spanish city of Ceuta, in the midst of a migration crisis.

"To be honest, I didn't really understand what was on the shirt," Konaté said on Tuesday. "You have to understand, I'm from France, but my parents came from Africa. Many things happen, and many people are in the same situation as me... In that situation, I didn't understand what it meant on the shirt, and I was focused on the game."

articles.headline: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 7: From Eagles to Matthew Stafford
articles.description: Get ready for Week 7 with takes on the Colts' decision-makers, Caleb Williams' MVP case, Matthew Stafford's play, the Browns' trajectory and the Eagles' next moves.
articles.body:
Are you excited for NFL Week 7? 'Thursday Night Football' between Bears QB Caleb Williams and Patriots QB Drake Maye is a great "future of the league" contest. Bengals at Ravens will always be a banger ... if QB Lamar Jackson is active. Chiefs at Seahawks on Sunday night will either right the Seattle ship or make the alarm bells scream.

Every Tuesday of the NFL season, I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide'

This week, I'll start with some reactions to the biggest Monday news -- Jalen Hurts being placed on season-ending injured reserve and the firing of Colts general manager Chris Ballard -- before peeking at what's going wrong in Los Angeles and what's going right in Cleveland, of all places.

Jump to:

Colts are right to keep Steichen

Eagles should make three trades

Williams should be MVP candidate but ...

Simmons for Defensive Player of Year

Cleveland is a QB away from contending

Stafford's age is starting to show

Some extra inklings

I think ... Carlie Irsay-Gordon was right to give Shane Steichen more time

The Colts (2-4) fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday following their Week 6 loss to the Titans (1-5). That's the thing about home losses to winless divisional rivals: They spur swift corrective action.

Interestingly, head coach Shane Steichen was not fired midseason alongside Ballard. As owner Irsay-Gordon said in her statement released by the Colts: "This does not change our goals for this season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect to compete, improve and win football games." There's a clear message to Steichen in this final line -- that she is leaving the door open for him to coach his way into another year on the job.

Just how many wins that might take is unclear. ESPN's Football Power Index gives the Colts an 8.8% chance to make the postseason -- something they have not done since 2020. Is Steichen's percent chance to save his job -- 1 in 12 -- about the same?

No matter the size of the crack in the door, I think this is a sharp call by Irsay-Gordon. While midseason coach firings shake up the game-day result more than midseason general manager firings, the primary brunt of the blame in Indianapolis rests with Ballard. Since Andrew Luck's' surprising retirement in 2019, the Colts have ridden a carousel of veteran stopgaps at QB -- Philip Rivers, Jacoby Brissett, Carson Wentz, Matt Ryan, Gardner Minshew II and Daniel Jones -- with one huge swing-and-miss at the draft plate in Anthony Richardson Sr.

articles.body:
The fantasy football strength of schedule cheat sheet is a breakdown of each team's remaining schedule and rank how easy/hard their collective opponents are in terms of allowing fantasy points to each offensive position: quarterback, running back, wide receiver, tight end, D/ST and kicker. 

This tool can help inform your waiver wire and trade decisions, or assist you in making those tough weekly lineup decisions, but please note that they are already factored into the weekly projections.

"YTD" represents how easy/hard each team's schedule has been thus far. "ROS" indicates how easy/hard each team's schedule will be moving forward, through the end of Week 17. The lower numbers, in green, are for the easier matchups.  Higher numbers, in red, are harder.

articles.headline: Fantasy football: Live Week 7 free agent pickups advice with ESPN expert
articles.description: ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody is here to answer your pressing questions live from noon to 1 p.m. ET.
articles.body:
Join the chat as ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody will be here to answer all of your waiver wire questions and other fantasy-related queries, live from noon to 1 p.m. ET every Tuesday of the NFL's regular season. 

Which surprises from last weekend's games are worth picking up in your league? Should you drop the player that has disappointed you so far? Should you be considering a trade to upgrade your roster? Ask away! Our expert will try to answer as many questions as he can to get you ready for this week's action. 

More advice: Week 7 free agent pickups | Week 7 rankings

Why is my question not getting answered?

Once submitted, your question does not automatically get posted in the chat. Our moderators select which questions they wish to answer and are trying to avoid repeat questions or topics. Scroll back to see if perhaps your question (or one very similar) was answered earlier in the chat.

We are receiving thousands of questions during our hourlong Q&A session and try to get to as many as we can. However, while we appreciate every submission, there is no way we can get to every question that comes in.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Premier League clubs eye Alexander-Arnold amid Real Madrid uncertainty
articles.description: Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold is considering his future at the Bernabéu, with Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Man City monitoring his situation. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester City are keeping an eye on the situation of Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold, while Barcelona and Bayern Munich are scouting Aston Villa attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold is considering his future at the Bernabéu, with Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester City monitoring his situation, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old is frustrated with limited playing time under José Mourinho, having made just three LaLiga starts this season amid competition from Denzel Dumfries, while his former club Liverpool are looking for reinforcements at right back following Jeremie Frimpong's injury. Meanwhile, Madrid are closing in on an official announcement for a new one-year contract extension with 34-year-old goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, reports Fabrizio Romano.

- Barcelona and Bayern Munich are scouting Aston Villa attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi following his strong start to Premier League life, TEAMtalk reports. The 21-year-old, who moved to the club from SC Freiburg for around £60 million this summer, has two goals and two assists in four matches, with Bayern viewing him as a target to explore if uncertainty grows over Michael Olise's future.

- Manchester United, Arsenal and Newcastle United are exploring a move for Roma full back Wesley, according to Football Insider. The 23-year-old's ability to play on both flanks has attracted interest from Old Trafford, though Roma are expected to demand a fee of €60 million to complete a deal.

- Chelsea are in contact with the representatives of AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott ahead of a potential January approach, Fabrizio Romano reports. With the Cherries unable to reach an agreement on a contract extension with the 23-year-old, they could let him move during the winter window, though any deal is expected to require an offer of at least £100 million.

- Manchester United have made contact regarding Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha, with Liverpool also showing interest, according to TEAMtalk. The 26-year-old Germany international is viewed by the Reds as an alternative target to Bournemouth's Scott, who (as above) could move to Chelsea.
